notes.title: Frequently Asked Questions
notes.notes: [p][i]How long is the game?[/i][/p][p]The game is approximately 15 hours long.[/p][p][/p][p][i]Do I need to play the first game?[/i][/p][p]While not required, completing [i]Elohim Eternal: The Babel Code[/i] is recommended for a fuller experience. Unlike video game series such as [i]Final Fantasy[/i] and [i]Tales of...[/i], the [i]Elohim Eternal[/i] series follows an overarching plot (similar to the [i]Trails of Cold Steel[/i] series); however, each game in the series does present its own complete story. The game also features a "What Comes Before" feature so you can learn what occurred in games preceding this one. [/p][p][/p][p][i]What other games are in the series?[/i][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45393696/972abdfbbc5edb22149183a986dff01178795c8a.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][i]I like story-driven games, will this scratch the itch?[/i][/p][p]Definitely. This is a story-first game, reminiscent of the era Xenogears came out. However, if you do not like story in your games…please, please, please do not purchase this. This game is not for you.[/p][p][/p][p][i]I’m religious—will this offend my religion?[/i][/p][p]No. This game is meant to be pro-religion without being preachy. The game uses many religious symbols with a purpose (albeit, that purpose is mostly implied rather than explicit). Note that this is a fictional story and allegorical – it is not, and should not, displace your place of worship or your religious texts. I myself am a Greek Orthodox Christian.[/p][p][/p][p][i]I’m not religious and have had bad experiences with religion—will this be triggering or offensive?[/i][/p][p]No. This game invites people from all walks of life. While it uses Judeo-Christian symbolism at its core, it does not require an understanding of those beliefs. It is also not intended to be preachy. Rather, it is intended to have you ask questions, perhaps get interested, and seek that knowledge and research on your own should you choose to go down that path. Ultimately, the overall story—about hope, struggle, and sacrifice—is one we can all relate to regardless of creed.[/p]

notes.title: Azar Combat
notes.notes: [p]Elohim Eternal II: Son of Man marks the first time in the series players will have access to and be able to customize their azars.[/p][p]Azars are mecha—think gears from Xenogears or skells from Xenoblade Chronicles X. Azars are powerful weapons with their own unique mechanics separate from ground units. [/p][p]Azar customization is more straightforward than with characters. You can upgrade your Azar’s attack core, armor core, and boost core to improve their attack, defense, and agility. Some cores will increase different types of attack or defense, like physical versus aether attacks and defenses. [/p][p]You can also equip your azar with two programs. Programs provide the azar with additional skills outside of their astar abilities. Specifically, programs provide the azar with support or control skills, such as buffing azars, repairing azars, and debuffing enemy azars. [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45393696/4f021003abfcc277ed55b0c1f0f1ebdcdc2a60be.gif"][/img][/p][p]Azars also have access to astar abilities. Each azar can learn all the astars available, but can only equip a fixed number of astar abilities. These abilities include physical attacks, aether attacks, super attacks, and shield-breaking attacks. There are various reasons for equipping different types of astars. For example, some astars may not provide much damage to the enemy but may increase tech points much faster, allowing you to then use a program or an aether attack that hits all enemy azars or hits one azar for high damage. [/p][p]Astar skills mostly cost aether points, but some cost both aether points and tech points. Programs only cost tech points. Azars also have large amounts of aether points, but skills cost more to use. Luckily, azars can use charge to refuel their aether points. [/p][p]Azar battles break up the combat mechanics of the game, providing something fresh to the experience. While most azar battles are story-driven, the player can challenge the azar arena where they will fight a series of increasingly difficult azar battles, putting to test their azar load outs. [/p]

notes.title: Combat - Ground
notes.notes: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45393696/26084e2e672592b85d29f1473d335db09c1e511a.png"][/img][/p][p]This post will go over the combat for ground units (when you’re not piloting an mecha azar). [/p][p]Elohim Eternal II: Son of Man’s combat system is inspired by Shin Megami Tensei with the player needing to take advantage of enemy weaknesses. [/p][p]Unlike the seven elements in [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1757890/Elohim_Eternal_The_Babel_Code/"]Elohim Eternal: The Babel Code[/url], there are four elements: Flare, Crystal, Nightfall, and Spark. Enemies can be weak to any one of these elements. As well, there are also physical weaknesses that enemies can be weak against, including Axe, Sword, Claw, Spear, Dagger, Whip and Staff. There’s also skills that are strong against archon-specific enemies and [i]only[/i] archon-specific enemies. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45393696/7ee0bc15e371899b4b3b33371c0df64cc22752e4.png"][/img][/p][p]Hitting an enemy weakness will give the player a chance to do extra damage through a simple quick-time event, similar to the Playstation classic Legend of Dragoon or the more recent Expedition 33. You can do double the damage to the enemy with this system. The player has a variety of options during combat. The player can use their consumables, like a scanner to scan enemy weaknesses (which do not cost a turn to do so). The player can also defend and reload their aether weapons (guns). [/p][p]The player will have use of one kinetic weapon (like a sword or dagger), two aether weapons (which cost aether points), and a heavy weapon. Players can mix and match different weapon types to fit their play style as well as cover the weaknesses. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45393696/75723e1c45e815c9259833b34898400243e0a7bd.png"][/img][/p][p]Players have Health Points (HP), Aether Points (AP), and Tech Points (TP). Health Points determines survivability (at zero HP and it's game over). All characters start off with only 3 Aether Points, but this can be increased with some accessories. Tech Points accumulate through battle and are needed to use heavy weapons. [/p][p]At the end of battle, Health and Aether Points are fully recovered, encouraging the player to use everything in their arsenal.[/p][p][/p]

notes.title: World & Lore
notes.notes: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45393696/20b851a0dec692ab45b4ead2df04993db1d56e7e.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Kenoma[/b][/p][p]Kenoma is one of two planets in the kosmeos. Kenoma is far more technologically advanced than its sister planet, Idin. It is also believed that the people on Kenoma have lived thousands of years before any life bloomed on Idin. [/p][p]Kenoma is the setting of Elohim Eternal II: Son of Man. It takes place about a thousand of years after [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3240300/Elohim_Eternal_Exodus/"]Elohim Eternal Exodus [/url]and at least 80 years after the events of [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1757890/Elohim_Eternal_The_Babel_Code/"]Elohim Eternal: The Babel Code[/url]. [/p][p][b]Pleroma[/b][/p][p]Pleroma is the central government of Kenoma. Pleromans are the elite class, including rich merchants, nobles, and royal guard. The Pleroman empire began with its matriarch, Empress Zipporah a thousand years ago. Today, the Emperor Tiberius reigns, though has not been seen in public for several years. All Pleromans know that it is Pontius Pilate that is pulling the strings of governance and control. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45393696/e320aeca877b8feb32d23c5120fcc48d743c60e0.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Shemer[/b][/p][p]Shemer is a lower class city, made up mostly of slums. The Shemerians, while part of Kenoma, are not considered Pleromans, but beneath Pleromans. Because of this status, Shemer is under the oppression of the Pleroman government. [/p][p][b]Monad, Demiurge and the Messiah[/b][/p][p]The One True Monad is believed to be the Creator of the kosmeos, the Kingdom of Heaven, and everyone in it. However, it is believed that the Demiurge, a couple known as Theletos and Sophia, usurped the throne of the Kingdom of Heaven from their creator, the One True Monad. It is also said the One True Monad will one day send a Messiah that will save the people of Kenoma from the Demiurge. Shemerians believe that the Messiah will also bring peace and elevate the Shemerians. [/p][p]The Pleroman government has been working towards waging war on the Demiurge to reclaim the Kingdom of Heaven. [/p][p][b]The Desert of Dudael[/b][/p][p]The Desert of Dudael is a vast, uninhabitable desert. It is where monsters known as archons dwell. Kenomans—mainly Shemerians—who have fallen so far from the grace of the One True Monad may mutate into an archon. [/p][p][b]Sanctuary[/b][/p][p]Sanctuary is a place where Pleromans send Shemerians on the verge of becoming archons to receive treatment and rehabilitation. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45393696/ad7fd7bd6168542acb97eb50dd410511280bffa1.png"][/img]  [/p][p][b]Zealots[/b][/p][p]The zealots are a group of Shemerians that fight against the corruption of the Pleromans. They seek to overthrow the current government. The zealots were once a force to be reckoned with, but were decimated after the Time of Tribulation.[/p][p][b]Time of Tribulation[/b][/p][p]The Time of Tribulation was a tragic, punishing event that saw many Shemerians—men, women, and children—massacred by Pleroman forces. The massacre was due to the zealots plan for rebellion. It was the Time of Tribulation that saw the zealot forces reduced to ashes. Many were slaughtered or captured; many lives changed irrevocably. To this day, it is unclear who betrayed the zealots to the Pleromans, for it seemed as though the Pleromans knew exactly where the zealots were and what they were planning. [/p]
